title: “All conditioned things are impermanent” — When one sees this with wisdom, One becomes disenchanted with suffering — This is the path to purity. “All…
content:
“All conditioned things are impermanent” —
When one sees this with wisdom,
One becomes disenchanted with suffering —
This is the path to purity.

“All conditioned things are suffering” —
When one sees this with wisdom,
One becomes disenchanted with suffering —
This is the path to purity.

“All phenomena are not-self” —
When one sees this with wisdom,
One becomes disenchanted with suffering —
This is the path to purity.

title: “Monks, there are these three unwholesome thoughts: sensual thought, ill-will thought, harmful thought. And these three unwholesome thoughts are abandoned without remainder in one whose…
content: “Monks, there are these three unwholesome thoughts: sensual thought, ill-will thought, harmful thought. And these three unwholesome thoughts are abandoned without remainder in one whose mind is well established in the four foundations of mindfulness or who develops the signless concentration. Monks, develop the signless concentration well. When the signless concentration is developed and cultivated, it brings great fruit and great benefit.”

title: Who once was heedless, but later is not, Illuminates this world like the moon freed from clouds. Whoever stops an evil deed by a wholesome…
content:
Who once was heedless, but later is not,
Illuminates this world like the moon freed from clouds.
Whoever stops an evil deed by a wholesome one,
Illuminates this world like the moon freed from clouds.

title: “Aggivessana, what is untrained body and untrained mind? Here, Aggivessana, an untaught ordinary person experiences a pleasant feeling. Having felt that pleasant feeling, he lusts…
content: “Aggivessana, what is untrained body and untrained mind? Here, Aggivessana, an untaught ordinary person experiences a pleasant feeling. Having felt that pleasant feeling, he lusts after it and falls into lust for pleasure. If that pleasant feeling ceases, and due to its cessation, a painful feeling arises, he sorrows, grieves, laments, beats his breast, and becomes distraught. Aggivessana, that pleasant feeling arises for him and invades his mind and remains because the body is untrained. That painful feeling arises and invades his mind and remains because the mind is untrained. In this manner, for a person in whom either way — pleasant feeling arises and invades his mind because the body is untrained, and painful feeling arises and invades his mind because the mind is untrained — he is one with untrained body and untrained mind.”

title: Elder Mahā-Moggallāna: All conditioned things are impermanent — Having arisen, they must cease. After arising, they cease — Their calming is bliss. Those who see…
content:
Elder Mahā-Moggallāna:

All conditioned things are impermanent —
Having arisen, they must cease.
After arising, they cease —
Their calming is bliss.

Those who see the five aggregates
As other, not-self,
Penetrate the subtle,
Like a dart piercing a hair-tip.

Those who see the formations
As other, not-self,
Penetrate the subtle,
Like a dart piercing a hair-tip.

As if struck by a sword,
As if his head were on fire,
Mindful, a monk should go forth,
Abandoning sensual lust.

As if struck by a sword,
As if his head were on fire,
Mindful, a monk should go forth,
Abandoning craving for existence.

Not with such weakness,
Not with such little strength,
Can one attain Nibbāna,
Liberation from all bonds.

This young monk,
This supreme man,
Conquering Māra and his army,
Bears this last body.

title: “Householders, those venerable ascetics and brahmins do not see the peril, the degradation, the defilement of unwholesome states, nor the escape, the benefit, and the…
content: “Householders, those venerable ascetics and brahmins do not see the peril, the degradation, the defilement of unwholesome states, nor the escape, the benefit, and the purification of wholesome states.”

title: “And what, monks, is restraint? Monks, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable … enticing. If a monk does not delight in…
content: “And what, monks, is restraint? Monks, there are forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable … enticing. If a monk does not delight in those forms, does not praise them, and dwells without lust for them, then that monk, monks, should understand: ‘I have not fallen away from wholesome states.’ The Tathāgata calls this ‘not falling away.’ … There are sounds … odors … tastes … touches … There are phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable … enticing. If a monk does not delight in those phenomena, does not praise them, and dwells without lust for them, then that monk should understand: ‘I have not fallen away from wholesome states.’ The Tathāgata calls this ‘not falling away.’ Thus, monks, is restraint.”

title: “If there is form, Rādha, then there is death, or a killer, or being killed. Therefore, Rādha, you should see form as death, see it…
content: “If there is form, Rādha, then there is death, or a killer, or being killed. Therefore, Rādha, you should see form as death, see it as a killer, see it as being killed, see it as a disease, see it as a boil, see it as a dart, see it as misery, see it as its own misery. One who sees form thus sees rightly.”

title: “A boil, monks, is a synonym for this body composed of the four great elements, born of mother and father, nourished with boiled rice and…
content: “A boil, monks, is a synonym for this body composed of the four great elements, born of mother and father, nourished with boiled rice and porridge, impermanent, subject to rubbing, pressing, breaking, dissolution, and destruction. It has nine wound openings, nine natural orifices. From these, whatever flows out is inevitably impure, foul-smelling, and disgusting; whatever issues out is inevitably impure, foul-smelling, and disgusting. Therefore, monks, be disenchanted with this body.”

title: “Monks, you should train thus: ‘Our minds will be trained and accumulated as when we went forth; unarisen unwholesome states will not overcome our minds…
content: “Monks, you should train thus: ‘Our minds will be trained and accumulated as when we went forth; unarisen unwholesome states will not overcome our minds and persist; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of impermanence; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of not-self; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of foulness; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of peril; having known the world’s even and uneven, our minds will be trained and accumulated with that perception; having known the world’s arising and passing away, our minds will be trained and accumulated with that perception; having known the world’s origination and cessation, our minds will be trained and accumulated with that perception; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of abandoning; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of dispassion; our minds will be trained and accumulated with the perception of cessation.’ Thus, monks, you should train.”
